title: Design an ML Feature Store
prompt: Design a feature store that lets ML teams define features once and use them consistently for both offline model training (large batch reads over historical data) and online inference (single-entity lookups with very low latency).
requirements: Functional: register a feature definition, compute/materialize feature values, serve them for batch training jobs and for real-time inference lookups

Non-functional: online lookups need single-digit-millisecond latency; offline training needs to efficiently read large historical windows; training and serving must use the same feature values to avoid skew
discussion_points: Separate storage paths for the online store (low-latency point lookups) vs. the offline store (large batch scans), and how they stay consistent
Point-in-time correctness for training data — avoiding leaking future information into a feature value used for a past training example
Feature computation: batch/streaming pipelines that keep the online store fresh
Training/serving skew: what causes it here and how the design prevents it
How a new feature gets backfilled over historical data without disrupting live serving
Multi-tenancy: many teams sharing the feature store without stepping on each other's compute or feature namespaces
